title: Control of Cell Geometry through Infrared Laser Assisted Micropatterning
protocol: Prepare squeaky-clean coverslips as described in Waterman-Storer, 1998.
Incubate coverslips in a 1% (3-aminopropyl)trimethoxysilane solution for 10 min with gentle agitation.
Wash coverslips twice with dH2O for 5 min each.
Incubate coverslips in a 0.5% glutaraldehyde solution for 30 min on a shaker.
Wash coverslips three times with dH2O for 10 min each.
Spin dry coverslips for 30 s using a custom-built coverslip spinner.
Store activated coverslips at +4 °C in a box with dividers for up to one month.
Mix PVA (98% hydrolyzed, MW 98000) with dH2O to make a 5.6% solution.
Solubilize the mixture in a 90 °C water bath and immediately filter through a 0.2 µm filter while hot.
Store PVA solution at room temperature for up to 3 months.
Add one part HCl to eight parts PVA in a 15 mL tube.
Invert the tube carefully to mix the contents.
Pour 2 mL of the mixed solution into a 35 mm Petri dish.
Submerge a clean, preprocessed coverslip into the liquid in the Petri dish.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min on a shaker.
Carefully remove the coverslips from the solution.
Use the coverslip spinner to spin coat for 40 s.
Clean the tweezers.
Transfer the coverslip to a box.
Dry the coverslip at +4 °C overnight.
Turn on the microscope software.
Ensure that the "Apo LWD 25X/1.10W DIC N2" objective is mounted on the microscope.
Set the laser line to 750 nm in the A1plus MP GUI window.
In the Calibration tab, click on New Optical Configuration.
Name the optical configuration "Image".
Leave all other options as default and select the appropriate objective.
Click on the Settings button to configure hardware settings under this optical configuration.
Set the Stimulation Laser to IR stim.
Place the Beam Splitter (BS 20/80) in the light path.
Set the Scanner Unit to Galvano and select the appropriate descanned detector.
Select a scan size and dwell time that is sufficient to capture small features on the coverslip.
Click on the Normal button so no line averaging or line integration is performed.
Check the Use IR Laser box.
Set up unidirectional scanning for simplicity.
Adjust laser power to 3 - 5% of the maximum power.
Adjust detector sensitivity ("HV" slider) to 15 V.
In the A1plus Scan Area window, set Zoom to 1 to capture the entire FOV.
Duplicate the "Image" optical configuration and rename it "Print_Fudiciary_Marker".
Select the smallest scan size and dwell time in the A1plus Compact GUI window.
Set detector sensitivity to 0.
Increase laser power to 30%.
Set Zoom to maximum (15.87) in the A1plus Scan Area window.
Place the scan area in the middle of the FOV.
Set up a Z-stack experiment in the ND Acquisition window.
Select Relative movement in the Z position and appropriate Z device.
Set step size to 2 µm.
Set stack depth to 10 µm above and below.
Duplicate the "Image" optical configuration and rename it "Autofocus".
Decrease Zoom factor so the FOV is slightly larger than the fiduciary marker.
Select Autofocus Set Up in the Devices menu.
Set scan thickness to that of the Z-stack experiment range.
Leave step size as default.
Duplicate the "Image" optical configuration and rename it "Load_ROI".
Set scan size identical to that of the ROI mask.
Duplicate the "Print_Fiduciary_Marker" optical configuration and rename it "Micropattern".
Set the Zoom factor to one.
Increase the stimulation laser power to ablate PVA.
Select an appropriate scan speed (40% and 32 s/frame in our experiments, respectively).
Enable StgMoveMainZ(-1.000,1) function before each phase.
Add a few phases to the Time Schedule and set each as Stimulation.
Ensure stimulation area and duration are correct.
Duplicate the "Print_Fudiciary_Marker" optical configuration and rename it "Label_Surface".
Increase laser power significantly in the A1plus Compact GUI window and set Zoom to one.
Generate a 2048 × 2048 RGB image using Adobe Photoshop or other available software with a black (0, 0, 0) background.
Draw 8 - 12 white (255,255,255) patterns on the black background.
Leave a 500 × 500 blank area in the center of the image for autofocusing.
Leave sufficient space between adjacent patterns (>200 pixels) and at the border of the FOV for optimal ablation and cell attachment.
Click on the Macro menu and select New Macro.
Import the "Pattern_Stimulation" code into the New Macro window.
Save the "Pattern_Stimulation" code to an appropriate folder.
Open another New Macro window and import the "Stage_Movement" code.
Ensure that the “Stage_Movement” working directory is identical to that in step 4.2.2.
Save the “Stage_Movement” code to the same folder as step 4.2.2.
Turn on the microscope and its accessories.
Ensure that the IR laser has warmed up sufficiently before use.
Transfer the PVA-coated coverslip onto a holder.
For an upright microscope, ensure the PVA surface faces down.
Add water to the corners of the coverslip to stabilize it.
Mount the holder onto the microscope stage.
Lower the objective and add water onto the coverslip.
Turn on the IR laser shutter in the A1plus MP GUI window.
Click on the Autoalignment button to align the laser prior to patterning.
Switch to the "Image" optical configuration.
In the A1plus Compact GUI window, click Scan to scan the FOV while slowly moving the objective closer to the coverslip.
Monitor the image brightness as the objective moves closer to the coverslip.
Move the objective until the image brightness increases and then decreases again, indicating the PVA surface to be patterned.
Focus on any small feature on the PVA surface and set zero on the Z drive.
Switch to the "Label_Surface" optical configuration.
Click on Capture.
Return to the "Imaging" optical configuration and scan.
Move the stage by 1 to 2 FOVs to avoid glass particles and scan to confirm.
Check that the objective is roughly in the center of the coverslip.
Ensure there is sufficient water between the objective and the coverslip.
Open the Stage_Movement macro from the Devices menu.
Set the variables "PatternLength" and "PatternHeight" to the desired number of FOVs for patterning.
Save and run the macro.
Switch to the "Imaging" optical configuration after patterning is complete.
Check that the IR laser shutter is open in the A1plus MP GUI window.
Move the stage to view the patterns.
Scan through the patterns to check their quality.
Transfer the coverslip to the grid box, with patterns facing up.
Store patterned coverslips at +4 °C for up to one week before use.
Make fresh 1 M NaBH4 in 1 M NaOH solution.
Add NaBH4 at a 1:100 ratio to pH 8.0 phosphate buffer containing 0.2 M ethanolamine.
Transfer patterned coverslips to a 35 mm tissue culture dish.
Incubate each coverslip with 1 mL of the solution above for 8 min to quench autofluorescence, and then rinse 3 times with PBS.
Dilute fibronectin (FN) in PBS to a final concentration of 10 μg/mL.
Incubate the coverslip in FN for 1 h at +37 °C.
Wash the coverslip 2 times with PBS.
Store in PBS at +4 °C overnight if not immediately used.
Culture a 10 cm dish of cells to 70% confluency.
Warm up cell culture media, PBS and 0.05% trypsin in a +37 °C water bath.
Relocate the patterned coverslip to a clean 35 mm tissue culture dish containing 1 mL warm PBS prior to seeding cells.
Aspirate the cell culture media from the 10 cm tissue culture dish and wash once with PBS.
Add 700 µL of 0.05% trypsin/EDTA to the dish.
Incubate the dish in a +37 °C, 5% CO2 incubator for 1 min.
Aspirate the PBS covering the patterned coverslip.
Add 1 mL of cell culture media to the coverslip.
Resuspend the detached cells with 10 mL of cell culture media.
Add 1 mL of resuspended cells to the patterned coverslip.
Culture cells in the incubator for 2 - 3 h.
Change media once to remove unattached cells.
Fix cells with 4% PFA in cytoskeleton buffer for 10 min at room temperature.
Follow immunofluorescence protocols established for the proteins of interest.
Acquire images of cells using an appropriate microscope.
Open the acquired images in NIS Elements and crop the images.
Install Anaconda and launch Spyder through Anaconda Navigator.
Download the script from Github and open it in Spyder.
Set parameters based on the acquired images.
Press F5 to run the script.
